articles.title: MLB Wild Card Round Day Three Game Thread
articles.summary: Someone’s season ends tonight
articles.body:
Only one game today, but it's a goodie. Winner-take-all. One team's season continues on to the next round to take on the Dodgers. The other begins their offseason far earlier than expected. We love do-or-die games here at Athletics Nation, and tonight's matchup between the Philadelphia Phillies and their division rivals the Atlanta Braves should be a great way to spend your Thursday evening.

The Braves have left-handed reliever Ray Ker (0-0, 1.97 ERA) opening the game for them tonight. He'll likely be only asked to handle the first inning or two before making way for the bulk pitcher, right-hander Grant Holmes (10-6, 3.44 ERA). The former A's prospect has blossomed with Atlanta over the past couple of years and now will be asked to soak up the middle innings of a must-win contest for his squad. No pressure.

Philadelphia meanwhile has a more standard approach to tonight's starter. They're sending out longtime Phillie Aaron Nola for the critical Game 3. The former Cy Young finalist is far past his heyday when he was constantly putting up ace-like numbers. While those days are long behind him he's still capable of tossing a gem every now and then. The Phillies need vintage Nola tonight if they want to advance to take on the Dodgers.

So who do you guys think wins tonight's contest? I'm taking Philly!

articles.title: Fast & Furious TV Show Greenlit at Peacock, With Vin Diesel as Executive Producer
articles.summary: The Fast & Furious films are getting their own television series, with none other than Vin Diesel himself serving as executive producer.
articles.body:
The Fast & Furious films are getting their own television series, with none other than Vin Diesel himself serving as executive producer.

As reported by Deadline on October 1, 2026, Peacock has officially given the green light for a Fast & Furious show. The series is slated to premier in 2028, the same year that the very last movie in the franchise is also set to release.

Vin Diesel first mentioned the show in May 2026 during a talk at NBCUniversal’s Upfront event, where he explained that fan demand drove Universal Pictures to consider expanding its high-octane IP.

Ranking the Fast and the Furious Movies: From Worst to Best

“As you all know, we are very precious about these movies but over the last decade, we’ve realized that the fans have wanted more, they wanted us to expand the legacy characters, their stories,” he said at the event. “And for the last decade, the desire has been for us to enter the TV space.”

Oh and of course, family was part of that decision: “That’s when I knew that the integrity of the characters, the international appeal, what makes us all feel like family will be protected in the TV space,” he added.

Mike Daniels (Sons of Anarchy, PONIES) and Wolfe Coleman (9-1-1: Lone Star) are both writers and co-runners for the show, which is one of four series planned for the Fast & Furious universe. As told by Deadline, one of these shows will be helmed by Nick Wooton (The Endgame) and Charmaine DeGraté (House of the Dragon), while the other two will be handled by Joe Henderson (Lucifer) and Ingrid Escajeda (Griselda).

With this in mind, it doesn’t look like the Fast & Furious world is set to end anytime soon, although its final film is on the horizon. This last movie, titled Fast Forever , is slated to release on March 17, 2028. It will mark the eleventh entry in the film franchise.

Vin Diesel spoke about the movie at Fuel Fest in June, where he detailed how he negotiated with Universal Pictures to bring its last adventure back to Los Angeles.

“The studio said to me, ‘Vin, can we please have the finale of Fast and Furious [in] April 2027?'” he told fans at the event. “I said, ‘Under three conditions.’ First, is to bring the franchise back to L.A.! The second thing was to return to the car culture, to the street racing! The third thing was reuniting Dom and Brian O’Conner.”

Given that O’Conner was played by the late Paul Walker, this statement led fans to wonder how the character will return. Walker’s brother was firmly against the idea of portraying his sibling in in Fast Forever, suggesting that AI could be used to bring him back to the franchise, instead.

articles.title: 8 Years Isn't Enough: Why This Console Generation Needs to Be Longer - Next-Gen Console Watch - IGN
articles.summary: Welcome back to Next-Gen Console Watch! This week Daemon, Ryan, and Max take a look at ex-PlayStation Worldwide Studios boss Shuhei Yoshida's recent comments about this current generation. Yoshida doesn't think gamers are interested in a PlayStation 6 or really any new generation of gaming hardware, and the PS5/Switch 2 generation should go for as long as possible. While our wallets might appreciate, can PlayStation's business model go beyond the usual 5-7 year lifespan of gaming hardware? articles.title: Dominic West and Sienna Miller Face Off as HBO’s New Legal Drama War Turns a High-Society Divorce Into Sleazy Fun
articles.summary: Our recap and review of HBO's War series premiere, starring Dominic West and Sienna Miller as a high-profile divorce erupts into a vicious legal battle.
articles.body:
Full spoilers follow for the season premiere of War.

HBO ’s slick new legal drama War will almost certainly be its next big water-cooler show, and deservedly so, as it’s a sharply written, deftly paced, and well-acted trashy delight.

The Season 1 premiere quickly establishes rival London law firms Cathcarts & Sons and Taylor & Byrne and their respective clients: social media mogul Morgan Henderson (Dominic West) and his movie star wife Carla Duval (Sienna Miller). Their long, now loveless marriage is basically over. So that means a very expensive and very public divorce will inevitably follow.

Carla not only wants out of the marriage, but she also wants to take Morgan’s fortune with her. But their pre-nuptial agreement is designed to keep Morgan bulletproof — provided he has lived up to his end of their bargain. He hasn’t. He’s been unfaithful to her before but this time Carla is armed with photographic evidence thanks to a honey trap .

Carla assures her lawyers she didn’t enlist her younger actress friend to sleep with Morgan but that doesn’t ring true. Her lawyers Serena Byrne (Phoebe Fox) and Nicholas Taylor (James McArdle), partners in both the firm and romantically, don’t like Carla’s underhandedness as it could be bad optics. Carla wants to file for divorce first but she and Taylor & Byrne are unaware that Morgan and his lawyers at Cathcarts have already deduced that she’s poised to file.

Beatrice “Queen Bea” Ubosi (Nina Sosanya) and St John Smallwood (Pip Torrens), Serena and Nicholas’ counterparts at Cathcarts, fire the first shot in this war by serving Carla divorce papers on the red carpet at the premiere of her new movie, a savage move reminiscent of Olivia Wilde being served onstage at CinemaCon . And Carla then has to smile for the cameras with Morgan at her side?! Ouch.

The episode’s biggest surprise, however, is saved for when we learn that the ambitious, overconfident young lawyer Johnny Warren (Archie Renaux) – newly hired by Taylor & Byrne specifically to work on Carla’s divorce – is, in fact, a mole working for Cathcarts. For the entire episode, we follow Johnny’s desperate search for a job at a law firm, so the reveal that he’s going to be the show’s equivalent of Matt Damon in The Departed is a fun twist.

Still, as a scrappy, lower class guy trying to make his way up the social ladder, Johnny is sympathetic — for now. Like Charlie Sheen’s character in Wall Street, the question remains just how much of his soul he’s willing to sell to succeed and how many personal relationships Johnny may destroy in the process. It’s a testament to the writing and to Renaux’s nuanced performance that the viewer remains invested in Johnny even when his arrogance gets the better of him.

War is impeccably acted across the board by an ensemble cast filled with familiar UK character actors playing the respective firms’ legal teams. As for the leads, West finds some sad-sack sympathy in his tech bro mogul, while Miller imbues Carla with a steely resolve that suggests she’d have been a natural fit in the boardroom had she not pursued acting. They’re only in one sequence together this episode but it’s rife with tension.

Showrunner George Kay’s finely tuned script is as darkly funny as it is sad in its portrait of the wounded (if not outright lost) humanity of its many characters, people who may not want to be this nasty but, well, that’s what you’re paid for, luv. I can’t wait to see what these posh bastards do next.

articles.title: Fortnite, Roblox, Minecraft and Steam must improve child safety, Australian report finds
articles.summary: Fortnite and Minecraft also told to 'lift their game' by online safety regulator.
articles.body:
Australia's online safety regulator has found "significant gaps" in how popular gaming platforms protect children online.

In a new report it found inconsistent approaches in how Steam, Roblox, Fortnite and Minecraft implement child safety measures as research shows nine out of 10 children aged 8 to 17 in Australia have played online games.

"Australian children have a right to play online without being exposed to predators, sexual extortionists, violent extremist content or other harmful material," eSafety Commissioner Julie Inman Grant said.

Roblox said it "prioritises the safety of our Australian community, especially the youngest users". The other platforms have been contacted for comment.

Weak safety on platforms allow "predatory adults" to make contact with children before grooming them, Inman Grant said, for sexual exploitation or radicalisation.

The report found that Valve - the US gaming giant that owns Steam and Steam Chat - was the only provider that did not use a type of technology widely used by the industry to detect and remove known harmful content.

Valve also did not "proactively" use tools to detect child sexual exploitation or violent material in chats, with current systems mainly flagging scams, the report found.

Roblox, along with Valve, were noted in the report as using only internal datasets to train language detection systems and for not regularly retraining these models.

"We expect these services to lift their game to identify and combat serious harms such as child sexual exploitation, sexual extortion and material and activity which promotes, incites or instructs violence," Inman-Grant said.

Minecraft and Fortnite, which does offer child accounts, generally let users self-declare their age, the report highlighted, meaning anyone who said they were adults could access "higher-risk communication features".

Steam also relied on users self-declaring their age but the report acknowledged the platform had recently introduced age checks using credit cards, and that Roblox had put in stronger age checks since last December.

Another issue raised by the report was the inconsistent manner in which the four gaming platforms shared information and participated in industry initiatives.

Mojang Studios, developer of Minecraft, and Roblox shared industry expertise in combating child sexual exploitation as well as violent extremism online, but Valve did not.

Elsewhere, Fortnite maker Epic Games failed to share instances of breaches with other platforms under a global programme that was designed to combat online child sexual exploitation and abuse.

The report was based on information collected by Australia's eSafety Commission on how the platforms were protecting users from serious online harm between October 2025 and March 2026.

Australia has made global headlines in recent years for its stance on online safety, after it introduced its world-leading social media ban for under-16s last December - which did not include gaming platforms - and a more recent push to force tech giants to offer users a chance to opt-out of social media algorithms .

A spokesperson for Roblox said it had "invested heavily" in its safeguards for children which include mandatory age checks.

Valve, Fortnite, and Microsoft - which owns Minecraft - have been contacted for comment.

Online gaming escaped Australia's social media ban - but critics say it's just as addictive

articles.title: Caitlin Clark struggled when it mattered most
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark and the Indiana Fever had championship aspirations heading into the 2026 season. Unfortunately, those championship dreams ended in the first ro...
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark and the Indiana Fever had championship aspirations heading into the 2026 season. Unfortunately, those championship dreams ended in the first round of the postseason as their superstar struggled when it mattered most.

On Thursday night, the Fever faced the Aces in a pivotal Game 3 showdown with the series tied 1-1. However, the Fever saw their season come to an end, falling 94-83 as Clark was not at her best in the pivotal game.

Given Clark's importance to the Fever, the team tends to go as she goes. When she is dominant, Indiana is dominant. When she struggles, however, it's often difficult for the team to overcome.

Unfortunately for both Clark and the Fever, she was not at her best this postseason, particularly in the Game 3 loss.

Clark finished Thursday night's game just 6-for-17 from the field and just 3-for-11 from three-point range. She also had six turnovers in the game with just four assists.

Clark's struggles were especially apparent in the fourth quarter. With the game on the line in the game's final period, Clark managed just two points, going 1-of-4 from the field with zero assists.

This was not the first time that Clark has struggled in the biggest games of the season. During the team's Game 1 loss to the Aces, Clark shot just 6-for-17 from the field and turned the ball over six times, though she also had 10 assists in the game.

It was a tall task to take on the league MVP and the defending WNBA champions in a series where Vegas had home court advantage. However, the Fever had a chance to secure home-court advantage and avoid this situation entirely, and Clark fell flat.

During the team's regular season finale against the Minnesota Lynx, the Fever had a chance to secure home-court advantage and earn a more favorable first-round matchup other than the Aces. It was a vitally important game, but unfortunately, Clark had the worst performance of her entire career, finishing with just two points in the game, going just 1-for-12 from the floor and with just three assists. The Fever star posted career lows in points (2), three-pointers (0), and field goal percentage (8.3%).

It's worth noting that Clark had a strong showing in Game 2 against the Aces, going 9-for-18 from the field with 27 points, 15 assists, and seven rebounds, going 5-for-11 from three-point range, but that performance was sandwiched between the two disappointing showings that led to Indiana's elimination.

Needless to say, it's been a rough stretch for Clark in some very pivotal games.

articles.title: Fever’s Caitlin Clark tips hat to Aces for championship mettle after Game 3 loss
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever were sent packing in the first round of the playoffs after losing to the Las Vegas Aces, 94-83, in Game 3 at Michelob ULTRA Arena. With bo...
articles.body:
The Indiana Fever were sent packing in the first round of the playoffs after losing to the Las Vegas Aces, 94-83 , in Game 3 at Michelob ULTRA Arena.

With both teams having their backs against the wall, the game remained close in the fourth quarter. The Aces, however, buckled up in crunch time to fend off the Fever and advance to the semifinals.

After the game, Caitlin Clark tipped her hat to the defending champions, as reported by ESPN's Michael Voepel.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"You've got to give credit to the Aces. I thought they played well. I thought they were ready to go, and that's what championship teams do," said Clark.

The 24-year-old guard struggled from the field, scoring 18 points on 6-of-18 shooting. She also had four assists, two steals, four blocks, and six turnovers.

Kelsey Mitchell also battled with inefficiency, scoring 23 points on 8-of-23 shooting. Aliyah Boston, meanwhile, tallied 19 points, 10 rebounds, three assists, and two blocks.

Indiana went 38% from the floor, including 9-of-32 from three-point range.

Clark was called for a technical foul in the first quarter after shoving Brianna Turner, who tried to listen to the Fever's huddle. Turner was also whistled for a technical foul.

Indiana entered the do-or-die affair with high confidence after beating Las Vegas in Game 2, with Clark exploding for 27 points, seven rebounds, and 15 assists. The defending champions, however, proved to be too much, led by the All-Star trio of A'ja Wilson, Chelsea Gray, and Jackie Young.

The Fever lost to the Aces in the playoffs for the second straight year.

articles.title: Aces Big 3 reigns supreme in win-or-go-home first round victory over the Fever
articles.summary: LAS VEGAS – A’ja Wilson just had that look in her eyes.
articles.body:
LAS VEGAS – A'ja Wilson just had that look in her eyes.

In fact, oftentimes it felt like there was nothing behind her eyes. She was all business. Minimal emotion. She clapped a couple of times and punched the air once — just to remind everybody whose house they're in. But nobody needed reminding.

Wilson bottled up the tough Game 2 loss to the Indiana Fever on Tuesday and moved on. Unlucky for the visitors, A'ja moving on was not good news.

The four-time MVP bounced back with fervor, producing a dominant 36-point, 10-rebound double-double in the Aces' gutsy 94-83 win-or-go-home Game 3 victory over the Fever Thursday night — punching the defending champions' ticket into their eighth consecutive WNBA playoff semifinal.

"I have my days, I have my moments, because I'm human," Wilson said. "But after a while I understood that I didn't want [the fan altercation in Game 2] to be a distraction, to myself or to my team, and I knew what we had to do coming into tonight."

Playing without late-scratch Stephanie Talbot (leg) and Dana Evans (knee), Wilson wasn't the only one who had a little extra on her plate tonight. However, she set the tone.

A'ja went a perfect 5-for-5 from the field in the first quarter, en route to 14 points. Caitlin Clark and the Fever kept pace, though. Clark scored 11 (4-7 FG), keeping the game tied at 31-31 through one.

The early stages suggested this game would be an all-out war, and it was. In the end, however, the ones who have won many deadly battles before prevailed once again.

Wilson added two blocks to her tally. Her forever running mates, Jackie Young and Chelsea Gray, played 40 minutes apiece, delivering 18 and 23 points, respectively.

Young flirted with a triple-double (eight rebounds, seven assists). Gray, 33, has nothing left to prove, but she didn't mind showing the world what she's all about again in the fourth quarter. She made clutch bucket after clutch bucket, producing 11 of her points. She chipped in five assists.

"I don't think I've played [Young and Gray] 40 minutes since I've been here," head coach Becky Hammon said. "I tried to use timeouts for rest, but it's just next woman up."

Unexpectedly losing key defender in Talbot last minute was a huge blow. But when times get rough, Hammon knows that she can always count on her star trio to go do what she always expects them to do. They combined for 77 points in this one.

"I needed them to go be the big three that I've always known them to be," she added. "And they deliver in big moments. … They're champions, and that's a spirit they carry with them. … If I'm looking across a line, I want to pick those three every time. … I'm proud of the group as a whole, but they're called the big three for a reason. And I had to ride them tonight."

The Fever never backed down. But there were moments throughout the game where it felt like perhaps the moment was getting a little big for them. The throne is difficult to get to and even more difficult to stay at. The Aces have proven the ability to do both, over and over.

That experience showed. The Aces couldn't relax right until the very end. But they closed the game out in true championship fashion. Hammon said on Tuesday that they would lean heavily on their pedigree tonight, and that they did.

The hosts took a narrow 70-65 lead into the fourth quarter — where they have been underwhelming most of the season — and they answered the bell when they really needed to, outscoring the Fever 24-18 down the stretch to hold on to the win.

Clark (18) and Kelsey Mitchell (23) were nearly impossible to contain in Game 2. The Aces, despite being shorthanded, were able to turn off the faucet on the dynamic duo at the perfect time.

Fever's backcourt combined for a respectable 41 points, but they were inefficient. They shot a combined 13-for-41 from the field and, more importantly, 6-for-23 from three-point range. Aliyah Boston added 19 points and 10 rebounds, but it was not enough to get over the Aces-shaped hump for a second year running.

Veteran Jewell Loyd earned the spot start in Talbot's place for Las Vegas, and although she was held scoreless in the second half, her 11 first-half points gave the Aces the juice they needed in key moments.

Loyd made three timely triples (3-6 3PT) and, more crucially for Hammon, held up defensively, having to replace an important contributor on that end of the floor. Talbot drew the Clark assignment in games one and two.

Hammon said that knowing who Talbot has to guard, she would only play if she was 100 percent. Loyd ensured that the drop-off in quality on that end of the floor was hardly noticeable. She's not new to this stage either, though the beginning did look a little shaky.

"She's Jewell Loyd. She has been in big games. She's a champion," Hammon said. "Even before [Talbot] went out, she was one of those primary defenders on [Clark]. So, she kind of just assumed her natural assignment. … After that first quarter, I thought it was going to be a long night. But we settled in, buckled in, and had a really great response — especially defensively."

The Aces' defense made the league's best regular-season offense in the Fever really uncomfortable, limiting them to just a 38.5 percent clip from the field and 28.1 percent from beyond the arc. Conversely, Vegas shot 45.3 percent from the field, 40 percent from three, and converted 28 of its 35 free throw attempts.

With her double-double, Wilson passed Tamika Catchings and Candace Parker for second-most in playoff history (28).

The likely soon-to-be five-time MVP, A'ja is averaging 32 points, 11.7 rebounds, two blocks, and 1.7 steals across the first three playoff games. She's shooting eye-popping 64.6 percent from the field and 66.7 percent from three — the latter development being a lethal weapon, making her virtually impossible to guard. She knocked down two of her three attempts from deep to close out Indiana (11-18 FG, 12-15 FT).

"Regular season is cute, it's so cute, everyone can come see us," she said in her post-game interview with the USA Network broadcast. "But this is the moment that we live for. So, for us to show up in these spaces and lean on each other and show resilience, that's something that you never get tired of."

And speaking of tiredness, Hammon is emphasizing rest and getting healthy in the upcoming days as the Aces now await their next opponent — the winner of Friday's Game 3 between the Golden State Valkyries and the Dallas Wings.

Game 1 of the semifinals is set for Sunday. Should the Valkyries win, the No. 3 seed Aces will be traveling to San Francisco this weekend. If the Wings pull off the upset, the Aces would host the opening two games of the semis and own home-court advantage for the remainder of the postseason.

But whoever it ends up being, the back-to-back and back again champions will be feeling really good about themselves after seeing off one of their fellow title favorites.

articles.title: Justin Wong and IFC Yipes Literally Commentate Ryu's Match Against Blanka in the Street Fighter Movie
articles.summary: We already knew about Justin Wong and IFC Yipes’ cameo in the upcoming Street Fighter movie, but it looks like they got to put their commentary skills to work for the part, too.
articles.body:
We already knew about Justin Wong and IFC Yipes’ cameo in the upcoming Street Fighter movie, but it looks like they got to put their commentary skills to work for the part, too.

Director Kitao Sakurai made sure the fighting game community felt represented in his Street Fighter film, inviting Justin Wong, IFC Yipes, and Maximilian Dood to play criminals in an apparent Shadaloo prison while Blanka (Jason Momoa) and Ryu (Andrew Koji) duke it out for M. Bison’s viewing pleasure.

These three community pillars were shown in a short teaser for the movie back in July. Come October 1, Wong shared some behind-the-scenes footage of his time on set, which included a closer look at the scene he shared with Yipes.

Hasbro's Street Fighter Figures: Image Gallery

Previously, we only saw the two fighting game pros-turned-commentators going bananas for Blanka and Ryu’s brawl; Wong’s footage shows himself and Yipes literally commentating the match, betting on commissary rations like ramen noodles and toilet paper.

It’s fantastic stuff, and it isn’t the only homage to the competitive scene that's included in the movie. Working with the makeup artists, Wong also gave his character a tattoo of the number 37 — and you can probably guess why he chose that particular ink. (He joked that his character had gotten sent to prison for stabbing someone who kept parrying him, saying, ‘You can’t parry a knife.’)

Speaking of Moment 37, Wong even got recognized by Noah Centineo (Ken), who asked which of the group was responsible for parrying Ken in “that sick-ass fight.” (Wong sheepishly admitted that he was the one who got parried, and later taught Centineo some moves in the game.)

All of the guest influencers got a tour of a few of the film’s sets, which included a look at some of the movie’s props. One of those props appeared to be Mike Haggar’s pipe, which would be an insane reference to include but not totally unexpected, given that Final Fight and Street Fighter take place in the same universe.

Street Fighter hurricane kicks its way into theaters on October 16, 2026. In the meantime, you can check out our interview with David Dastmalchian (M. Bison), who told us all about how he studied real-life dictators to bring Shadaloo’s leader to life.

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze .

articles.title: Avengers: Secret Wars Filming Delay Reports Spark Concern That Marvel's Multiverse Saga Finale May Be Postponed
articles.summary: Reports of an Avengers: Secret Wars filming delay have sparked concern among Marvel fans that the movie's release date could be pushed back.
articles.body:
Reports of an Avengers: Secret Wars filming delay have sparked concern among Marvel fans that the movie's release date could be pushed back.

This week, an array of Marvel movie insiders reported hearing that filming on Marvel's big Multiverse Saga finale will now begin later than planned, after previously being set to start last month.

Serial MCU tipsters Daniel Richtman , Alex Perez , and Apocalyptic Horseman appear to have independently verified that Secret Wars shooting will now take place early in 2027, likely in January, sparking concern among fans about the impact this hold up will potentially have.

Marvel Cinematic Universe: Every Upcoming Movie and TV Show

It's worth making clear that Marvel is yet to give any official update on its production schedule, and it ultimately may not need to do so if there's no impact on Secret Wars' planned December 17, 2027 launch date. That said, the potential of the movie's shooting schedule changing has many fans questioning if the film can still be completed in time.

"Gives the cast time to promote Doomsday during this winter," Marvel fan BTSMGL wrote in one of several lengthy threads on reddit . "I'm not in a rush for Ghost Rider so as long as we get X-Men and BP3 still in 2028, I'm fine with this."

"A *lot* is riding on Doomsday," added vadermaulkylo. "They’re probably waiting to see how it's received before committing to anything. If Doomsday gets a bad critical and/or audience reception then that'll drastically change what they'd do in its second act film."

"I'm getting tired of waiting," concluded own-papaya-4264. "Secret Wars was announced in 2022 for Christs sake."

Principal photography for Avengers: Doomsday lasted five months from April to September 2025, with additional material believed to have been recently shot ahead of the film's December launch. In other words, Marvel has had just over a year to work with the bulk of its footage in post-production.

Just for comparison, Spider-Man: Brand New Day was filmed between August and December 2025, for launch in July 2026. This is a much tighter turnaround of the kind fans now think Secret Wars will need, though Brand New Day is arguably a more straightforward project when compared to Avengers' enormous story scope and sprawling cast list.

Much remains unknown, including the exact date Secret Wars will now begin shooting, and whether Marvel has already banked footage it will incorporate into the movie while previously shooting Doomsday — a tactic used for Avengers: Infinity War and Endgame. Could Secret Wars get delayed? It's possible, though any sense that the film's launch could slip into 2028 would then likely impact the release of Marvel's three subsequent projects already scheduled for that year (X-Men, Ghost Rider, and Black Panther 3).

Still, if a delay is needed to ensure Secret Wars lands as Marvel hopes, a longer wait doesn't seem out of the question. Last month, directors Joe and Anthony Russo teased that Marvel fans need to prepare for "a very surprising ending" to Avengers: Doomsday , which has a "focused propulsive narrative," while still weighing in as one of the studio's longest films to date.

articles.title: The 10 Most Valuable Cards in Magic: The Gathering Reality Fracture
articles.summary: Here's our breakdown of the most expensive cards in Magic: The Gathering's brand-new expansion, Reality Fracture. That includes massive Facet Foil chase cards, $1,000 Echoverse hits, and a whole lot more to discuss.
articles.body:
Thanks to its packed release schedule, we’re only ever a few weeks away from a new Magic set in 2026, but after back-to-back Universes Beyond trips to the Marvel universe and back to Middle-Earth (and ahead of Star Trek in November), Reality Fracture offers something different.

A sort of “What If?” for the Magic multiverse, it showcases legendary Planeswalker Jace Beleren’s perfected “Echoverse”. Here, he’s reshaped reality to his will, and that means famous spells, creatures, and more are getting a revamp.

With prerelease weekend over, here are the most valuable cards from the set so far. As ever, prerelease pricing will change drastically at launch and in the days following. We’ll update this page again soon with the latest price updates.

Facet Foil is a new treatment for Reality Fracture, and it’s found on just about every card on this list that isn't in the Showcase treatment.

Rise of the Deathbringer kicks off our list as a five-cost instant that lets you draw cards in exchange for life, or reduce creatures by -3/-3. It’s currently going for around $200, but someone has already spent double that on it.

An echoverse of one of Magic’s most iconic mono-green cards, Craterclaw Colossus is a mono-red alternative to Craterhoof Behemoth.

As with its cousin, it’s a game-ender when played at the right time, offering haste and giving creatures you control trample, but it’s ramped up by the number of artifacts you have. This Facet Foil version is around $210 right now.

Remember Prepared spells from Secrets of Strixhaven earlier this year? Well, if you’ve been enjoying them regularly, then Codie, Ravenous Codex might be your next pick for a Commander.

Codie copies prepared spells, and for WUBRG, it can prepare all of your creatures. It’ll be fascinating to see the plays this leads to - it’s currently $300 for this Showcase Fracture Foil variant.

It’s Solemn Simulacrum for green, but Simulacrum Shaper could be just as valuable as its forebear. It nets you a basic land as it enters the battlefield and card draw when it dies, but also has typal synergy with Elf decks.

It’s currently $325 for the Facet Foil version, but the most recent sale is a whopping $499.99.

In the Echoverse, Strixhaven’s Elder Dragons have been reworked into Hexhaven’s Elder Sphinxes, and Kwia Vigorbloom is likely to be a popular one.

It’s a 6/6 with the keyword soup of flying, vigilance, lifelink, and ward 2. When you gain life, it creates Lotus tokens that can be sacrificed for three mana of any color, meaning if you can get Kwia Vigorbloom out nice and early, you’ll be able to ramp consistently.

It’s currently going for around $350, but this showcase version has already sold for over $400.

Emrakul, the Exigent Doom may just have the best name on this list, but it’s a fitting Echoverse version of an Eldrazi favorite.

This version of Emrakul untaps all lands you control, putting a 12/12 on the board with flying, trample, and a ward cost of sacrificing three permanents. You can even exile it from your hand to help ramp in the early game.

It’s going for $400 right now if you want this Showcase version in Fracture Foil.

Rise of the Dark Realms is a black staple in Magic, bringing all creatures from all graveyards under your control and (hopefully) ensuring a big win.

Return to the Light Realms is a little different. For one, it’s white, and for another, it’s all nonland permanents from your graveyard. Depending on how many artifacts, equipment, and enchantments you have in there, it might even be better than its predecessor.

This Facet Foil version will set you back $420 right now.

The Echoverse version of Rune-Scarred Demon drops from a 6/6 to a 4/4, switches from black to red, and lets you grab any card you want from your library before discarding a card at random.

In many ways, it’s not as good as its predecessor, but it does cost two mana less at least. It’s the first card on our list to hit $500.

Oh boy, this is the one I’ve had my eye on for a while. Hexhaven Invigorator is a four-cost green Chimera Horror. As it is dealt damage, you can convert that damage into lands - and they don’t have to be basic lands, either.

Add to that the fact that it’s a 6/6 with vigilance, so you’ll be swinging for big damage each turn, and this is a great mono-green inclusion. The Facet Foil is going for $562, but one has already sold for $850.

So what’s the most expensive card from the Reality Fracture set? Why, it’s the Echoverse version of Omniscience, of course.

Whereas its blue cousin lets you cast spells without paying their mana costs, this green version lets you cast spells with mana value less than or equal to the number of creatures you control without paying those costs.

Get a bunch of cheap tokens on the battlefield and then cast with reckless abandon. The Facet Foil version of Omnipresence is a whopping $1,000 right now.

MTG Reality Fracture is Selling Out Fast

Reality Fracture arrived in prerelease last weekend (September 26-27), with the full launch on October 2. Here's what you can still buy, and what's included.

Notably, Amazon is currently out of stock of everything Reality Fracture, so you may have to look elsewhere, like Walmart, Target, Best Buy, or resellers at TCGplayer, to find boosters or sealed boxes in stock.

Building out your collection is easiest with Play Boosters, and you can buy a box at Amazon for $164.70 .

This includes 30 packs, with Wizards of the Coast promising 60+ legendary cards per box. There are 14 cards per pack, so you’re getting a total of 420 in a box.

articles.title: Modder Deliberately Corrupts Their Own Hugely Popular Total War: Warhammer III Mod as Row Over AI Escalates
articles.summary: The creator of one of the most popular Total War: Warhammer III mods ever has deliberately corrupted it so that it will no longer work with “unauthorized reuploads,” amid a row over the rights and wrongs of AI-generated modifications.
articles.body:
The creator of one of the most popular Total War: Warhammer III mods ever has deliberately corrupted it so that it will no longer work with “unauthorized reuploads,” amid a row over the rights and wrongs of AI-generated modifications.

Veteran modder Venris has created Simply Fun Overhaul (SFO) mods for Total War: Warhammer for years, with a popular Patreon helping in the development of the latest version, SFO: Grimhammer III . The mod overhauls the base game to be closer to the lore and Warhammer universe, changing everything from the campaign and battle mechanics to the economy and customization.

Recently, people have used AI to release sub mods of SFO: Grimhammer III that work with updated versions of the main, Creative Assembly-developed video game, without asking permission. In response, Venris corrupted their own mod so that it stops working with these uploads, and threatened to make SFO: Grimhammer III private.

“Due to the growing number of unauthorized reuploads of SFO: Grimhammer III, and more importantly, the use of AI in the process, I have deliberately corrupted the mod to prevent it from functioning with such unauthorized uploads,” Venris said in a statement published online . “If this situation continues to escalate, I will make SFO: Grimhammer III private.

“SFO: Grimhammer is the result of nearly 10 years of passion and love for this community and the fantasy world. As such, I do not permit anyone to take my work without permission. Especially not for AI-related purposes.

Recent weeks have seen an explosion of AI-generated “mods,” which have called into question not just mod creation, but the very foundations of the video game industry. Clips of gameplay showing AI-generated “game-merging mods” have gone viral on social media, with others releasing AI-generated versions of games running on platforms they have yet to be officially released on. Some have used AI to add or expand features, increase player counts, or fuse parts of two different games together.

The mods have raised eyebrows online, and sparked questions about the legality of their release. Some within the traditional modding community have expressed shock and disappointment in AI-generated clones and mashups, and have questioned the continued viability of their hobby.

For video game publishers, the potential impact may be existential. Why buy a new Fallout video game if AI can spit one out for you in a matter of minutes? This week, the person behind a viral AI-generated Fallout: New York game pulled it offline after receiving a cease and desist from Bethesda , leading fans to celebrate.

But not all oppose AI-generated mods, clones, or video games. “Oh no the horror,” one person said in response to Venris’ post. “Someone forget to get a rubberstamp from a bureaucrat modder whose work depends on the original game devs and publishers anyway. You guys are such losers.”

Most, though, have backed Venris on this. “Anyone that thinks that you are doing something bad here doesn't have experience with someone stealing something that they have spent a major chunk of their life making and it shows,” one person said.

articles.title: With a Smirk, Robert Pattinson Calls Michael Bay's Transformers 'The Definitive Movie of the 2000s'
articles.summary: On YouTube show The List, presented by movie publisher A24 and Letterboxd, Robert Pattinson and Lance Oppenheim chatted about their favorite movies. During the chat, Pattinson namedropped Michael Bay’s Transformers as “the definitive movie of the 2000s.”
articles.body:
On YouTube show The List , presented by movie publisher A24 and Letterboxd, Robert Pattinson and Lance Oppenheim chatted about their favorite movies. During the chat, Pattinson namedropped Michael Bay’s Transformers as “the definitive movie of the 2000s.”

The pair opened up the show talking about movies with bright, saturated colors and glossy tones. According to Pattinson, this style of color grading culminated in Transformers and was never seen again.

Robert Pattinson, of course, is a little scamp. You never know when he’s telling the truth or playing with the audience. Famously, he once lied in an interview about witnessing the death of a clown. As he called out Transformers as the definitive movie of the 2000s, he had the same evil smile on his lips as the clown interview.

Elsewhere in the interview, Pattinson praised Scarface for its balletic action scenes, while Oppenheim said he can tell if he’s going to like someone depending on if they like Tom Cruise movie Vanilla Sky or not.

According to Oppenheim, Pattinson often texts him one word: “Braveheart.” “Think Braveheart.” Pattinson called that movie's famous “you’ll never take our freedom” speech out as one of his favorite movie moments.

The pair were on the show to promote Primetime , a psychological thriller in which Pattinson plays To Catch a Predator host Chris Hansen. The film’s opening weekend raked in $19.2 million from 2,863 theaters, ranking third in A24’s library, behind Backrooms ($81.4 million) and Civil War ($25.5 million).

IGN's 9/10 Primetime review praises Robert Pattinson for setting "the screen ablaze as a heightened, petulant Chris Hansen." Chris Hansen, the subject of Primetime, called the movie a "fever dream" and has promised to make his own documentary in response.

Pattinson is currently filming The Batman Part 2 , which he teased "goes in a completely different direction" to the first movie. Due to the menacing nature of his Primetime character, fans have been asking Pattinson to play The Joker alongside his Batman appearance.

Elsewhere, Pattinson cast doubt on fans hoping to see his dark and gritty take on the Caped Crusader in James Gunn's wider DC universe . "It's such a specific kind of [style], the tone of it gets inside you," he said.

As for Transformers, the Transformers and G.I. Joe crossover movie is now canceled, although Bradley Cooper will star as Duke in a standalone G.I. Joe movie directed by Danny McBride.

articles.title: Star Wars: Galactic Racer Video Review - IGN
articles.summary:
Star Wars: Galactic Racer reviewed by Luke Reilly on Xbox Series X. Also available on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series S, and PC.
"Star Wars: Galactic Racer is a fabulous looking and frantically fast anti-grav racer that impressively goes further than just taking the decades-old Star Wars Racer games and giving them a 4K facelift. With a range of satisfyingly customisable vehicle classes beyond podracers, a world outside the racing you can soak in and explore in third-person, and an interesting roguelite-adjacent structure that injects a considerable degree of risk into the action, Galactic Racer is a fresh and accomplished blend of Lucas lore with the destructive spirit of arcade racing icons like Burnout and MotorStorm. Its run-based campaign can grow unavoidably tedious over long stints because of its heavy reliance on repeatedly revisiting the same slim selection of planets, and its lack of splitscreen is disappointing considering its roots run back to consoles regarded as the kings of same-couch chaos. But Galactic Racer is an otherwise confident debut from developer Fuse Games, and one that has successfully lit the afterburners on a long-dormant slice of the Star Wars universe."

articles.title: Star Wars: Galactic Racer Review
articles.summary: Star Wars: Galactic Racer is a fabulous looking and frantically fast anti-grav racer that gets a little repetitive thanks to its heavy reliance on repeatedly revisiting the same slim selection of planets, but has successfully lit the afterburners on a long-dormant slice of the Star Wars universe.
articles.body:
For a series as storied as Star Wars – one brimming with more spacecraft and speeders than George Lucas has beard bristles – it borders on baffling that developer Fuse Games’ Star Wars: Galactic Racer can arrive in 2026 as the first new game of its kind in over two decades. I blame Super Bombad Racing, if only because Gungan isn’t a real language and using a portmanteau of bomb and bad in the title was probably never the perfect pathway to sales success. Galactic Racer, on the other hand, has a range of impressively customisable vehicle classes that expands the hangar well beyond classic podracers, gorgeous course design, and an impressively credible and explorable world outside the on-track action. It’s an eye-catching and rich resurrection of Star Wars racing that’s as fast as it can be surprisingly unforgiving.

Galactic Racer’s main hook is its run-based, roguelite-inspired campaign, which comes with a strict philosophy of no mid-race restarts. It is an interesting and genuinely fresh approach that bakes a very real and logical feeling of risk and danger into the action – a feeling that is admittedly absent in racing games with any sort of rewind functionality or unlimited restarts. Yes, you can still pause and, yes, you can still save and come back later – but you otherwise need to live with the consequences of what happens out on the track. It’s a structure that makes the racing tense and meaningful, even if racing over the same landscapes over and over does grow repetitive.

Whether by intent or not, the huge time gap between Galactic Racer and classic Star Wars games like Episode I: Racer and Racer Revenge feels almost mirrored in Fuse Games’ original story. That is, where those games were set in the prequel period, Galactic Racer is set in the aftermath of Return of the Jedi, where the art of podracing is a distant relic of a bygone era. Unsurprisingly, podracing does still feature here, and it’s represented incredibly; lightning quick, and with impeccably authentic sound design. However, I’m hesitant to describe specifically how or when it pops up outside of the quickplay modes. Just know that I feel like the Fuse Games crew were paying close attention when Maverick found an F-14 in the heart of enemy territory during the Top Gun sequel, or when Bond retrieved his DB5 in Skyfall. I may be a pretty casual Star Wars fan by most metrics, but I do love stuff that imbues vehicles with a sense of old soul – even fantasy ones. That’s my jam.

For clarity, the bulk of the Galactic Racing League garage consists of landspeeders, speeder bikes, and a new vehicle type called skim speeders. Bikes are fast but fragile, and skim speeders have a podracer-esque ability to bank completely vertically to slice through gaps and turn harder, but landspeeders have proven to be my favourite class. They’re essentially floating cars, and I enjoy their more predictable handling and added durability.

As the mysterious and faceless human racer called Shade, our ultimate goal is to beat the Galactic Racing League’s moaning, arrogant, and entitled heel Kestar Bool in the final head-to-head race. However, for that to happen, we need a suitably fast vehicle. In simple terms, building and piloting a quick one requires a combination of general stat upgrades, performance parts, and various additional perks – from gadgets that can be activated during races to specific bonuses granted to you by allies you accumulate over the course of the story. These are rationed out randomly, or earned, as we progress (and re-progress) through the championship “tours.” I’ve grown to be a particular fan of the autopilot gadget, which is regularly a lifesaver to tackle particularly treacherous stretches of track. The fact that these gadgets are primed just prior to race starts with a series of specific button presses, like pre-flight checks, is a very clever touch that gives waiting on the grid a tangible sense of occasion. The sequence always ends with the final go-ahead to fire your engines, which cough to life and glow harder as you squirt the throttle. It was important to somebody at Fuse Games that we should be able to rev our speeders like hotrodders at a red light, because it looks cool. I love little flourishes like that.

Now, speeders are scrapped between tours, so you’ll need to choose and set-up a new one each time. It’s not a solution I find I’m loving, considering I was never able to establish any real sense of ownership or attachment to a vehicle. Theoretically, you can build a replica of the same-looking vehicle every time – with the same add-on cosmetic parts and the same livery – but you will need to wave goodbye to specific upgrades you might’ve really enjoyed. The more heavily upgraded your previous speeder, the more points you’ll have to spend on pumping up its general stats before you start – but it won’t behave the same as your last one. Not unless you can pick up the same upgrades in your next run, whether by chance reward or spotting them in your mechanic Hibi’s randomised selection. As a roguelite rookie and a traditional racing game meathead, I have to admit I didn’t much like losing powerful upgrades that really suited my racing style to what’s essentially a dice roll, but I do appreciate the novelty of needing to come to grips with something not typical of the usual racers I play.

Tours unfold over three (and later five) planets before culminating in a final knockout event. Failing at any point means you’ll have to start a whole new one over again. This is quite elegantly and thoughtfully implemented, thanks to the racing paddock at each event you can fully explore in third-person. Not only does this build an authentic world around the Galactic Racing League – which in turn crafts a world I feel like I’m inhabiting, rather than just shuffling through menu screens – it lets Fuse Games fill it with characters that can acknowledge your previous failures as you return for another crack at the title. That is, you’re not actually restarting , or simply being scrubbed back in time until you get it right – time keeps moving forward and you just need to keep racing until you emerge victorious. The story is split into three distinct acts, so note that messing up in the third act means you’ll just need to take another run at the third act. That is, it doesn’t send us all the way back to the initial League qualification phase, and for that I’m grateful.

However, Galactic Racer’s core weakness is that it unfortunately doesn’t feature enough planets to avoid feeling overly repetitive. While I’m conscious a roguelite structure brings with it an expectation of a certain level of repetition, it does become fairly tedious slogging through its small list of repeating planets over successive attempts. The specific circuits used, the order of event types, and how they branch over the span of a championship are shuffled from tour to tour. There are reverse layouts for the tracks, too. However, the backdrops are nonetheless always the same. Having a couple more planets that could’ve been swapped in and out would’ve gone a long way in reducing the fatigue that quickly sets in after several runs through the same locations.

It is a fantastically realised array of planets, though, and the details of the track environments are as excellent as they are varied. Jakku, for instance, has routes traced through its immense graveyard of war wreckage – swinging from wide open blasts across debris-covered dunes one moment, to cramped sections of makeshift tunnels formed by half-destroyed spacecraft the next. Crait is characterised by sprawling caves and its flat, salt-covered surface – which speeders whip up to expose the red mineral beneath. Lantaana is covered in dense forest linked by lava tubes, and Sentinel I is a toxic wasteland where racers must negotiate narrow causeways over acidic pools.

Each planet and track has its own set of properties that can help you or harm you, depending on how you race and the upgrades you’ve applied. Perhaps my favourite example of this dynamic is Ando Prime, an entirely frozen planet, where heating tubes have been dropped sporadically around the circuits. Passing through these will thaw out the frozen control surfaces that numb your steering inputs, but staying out of these hot boxes allows you to run your delicate ramjet for much longer before it catastrophically burns out. It’s a racer that essentially never stops asking you questions.

Star Wars: Galactic Racer - June 2026 Screenshots

On the topic of burning out, it’d be massively remiss of me not to mention how much I adore the Burnout-inspired takedowns that Galactic Racer actively encourages, with speeders on the wrong side of a hefty slam being speared into trackside obstacles and splintering into thousands of shards. Not only are they incentivised with a slow-motion takedown camera, which swings back to soak in the spectacle, but they can be factored into the upgrade system. Any time I spot it on a run, I always opt to grab the upgrade that replenishes my speeder’s battery for each successful takedown – since doing so gives me more bursts of my autopilot ability.

But while the Burnout connection is strong (and hardly surprising considering the roots of Fuse Games’ founders reach back to Burnout creator Criterion Games), perhaps what I love most of all is how much Galactic Racer surprisingly reminded me of a sci-fi MotorStorm. That is, the often wide tracks full of natural obstacles and multiple routes, the multi-class nature of the grid, and the fact that holding onto that ramjet boost a fraction too long results in a fiery and rapid unscheduled disassembly. Funnily enough, just like the original MotorStorm, Galactic Racer also has no splitscreen multiplayer. 12-player online racing (or eight, for podracers) has a six-event championship structure that works a little like a shortened version of the singleplayer tours (where your upgraded vehicle is discarded after the finale) – but that’s for a different sort of player than me.

articles.title: Original Xbox Version of Halo: Combat Evolved Made Available to Play in a Browser
articles.summary: The original Xbox version of Halo: Combat Evolved has been made available to play in a web browser.
articles.body:
The original Xbox version of Halo: Combat Evolved has been made available to play in a web browser.

This is not a port of Bungie’s seminal 2001 first-person shooter, rather the original Xbox game running in your browser. Hot on the heels of decompilation work done elsewhere, AI developer Mitchell Hynes released Halo in a browser, hosting and maintaining the game himself.

Hynes made a point of explaining that this browser release is not Borderlands developer Gearbox's official and divisive 2003 PC port of Halo: Combat Evolved, no doubt to encourage veteran fans of the original to give it a shot. And his tweets appear to have gathered a great deal of attention. Five hours after releasing the game, it saw nearly 20,000 games, hitting an average of 94 frames per second.

Halo owner Microsoft may well take a dim view of the original Xbox Halo popping up in browsers, of course, despite the fact it’s free to play. Microsoft recently released Halo: Campaign Evolved on PC as well as consoles, and there can be no doubt that the company’s lawyers will see this browser version of the original as competition.

Indeed, some thought Microsoft had already taken action when Hynes’ website was flagged as “Suspected Phishing.” He insisted this was due to an automatic flag from Cloudflare, rather than Microsoft, and the ban was soon lifted.

We’re currently in the middle of an AI video game explosion that has seen various clips of famous games mashed together go viral as people use the likes of Claude to create “mods” much faster than previously possible. Some are using AI to create clones of famous games. Others are using AI to release versions of existing, traditionally made mods — much to their creators’ annoyance .

For video game publishers, the potential impact may be existential. Why buy a new Halo game if AI can spit one out for you in a matter of minutes? This week, the person behind a viral AI-generated Fallout: New York game pulled it offline after receiving a cease and desist from Bethesda , leading fans to celebrate. It will be interesting to see how long Halo in your browser stays online.

Meanwhile, Microsoft has handed the keys to the next mainline Halo game to Call of Duty company Activision, and gutted Halo Studios in the process.

articles.title: Ben Affleck Says There's 'Nobody Alive' Who Believes US Politics is Going Well — And Explains Why He Won't Personally Run for Office
articles.summary: Former Batman Ben Affleck has revealed the reason he won't run for political office, despite claiming there is a "collective disappointment" in how U.S. politics is currently trending.
articles.body:
Former Batman Ben Affleck has revealed the reason he won't run for political office, despite claiming there is a "collective disappointment" in how U.S. politics is currently trending.

Affleck is soon set to star in Animals , a political thriller for Netflix in which he plays a Los Angeles mayoral candidate involved in the criminal underworld.

Back in the early 2000s, Affleck occasionally expressed interest in following suit (minus the criminal underworld bit), but despite calls from many of his fellow cast members for him to genuinely pursue a political career, Affleck has now spoken out to squash the suggestion and reveal why he has no interest in public office — while simultaneously airing his unhappiness with the current state of the country.

"We don't ask the question of 'what are your qualifications to hold public office?' any longer," Affleck began, talking to Variety . "It's, 'You wanna join the circus? Who's the biggest carny?'

"Whatever side of the aisle you're on, one of the interesting things that people can agree on is a collective disappointment with the way that American politics has trended," the former Batman continued. "There's nobody alive now who thinks, 'hey, we're really doing it right and things are going great and I love this political system.' And that's a problem."

While declining to get into specifics, Affleck stated he could name "lots of things" he believes are wrong with the U.S., as well as fixes for them. Affleck has long been a Democrat party supporter, and has supported every Democratic presidential nominee since Al Gore back in 2000.

"The other thing is where you set up being politician and it's not about serving people, it's just about money, raising money," Affleck added. "It's just about playing a sort of adolescent game of who can make fun of the other person better or be more reductive and stupid about something rather than actually trying to talk about the issues.

"I think the thing that's missing from politics, frankly, is you have to lead. You can't just scare people. You can't just hector them. You can't lecture them. You can't guilt them into it. You've got to inspire them. Otherwise they don't want to vote for you."

So, why not go into politics? Affleck has now responded to say he was happy to stay as an actor, as "selfish" as this may be.

"Selfishly, I just see what a difficult grind of a job it is and I'd rather make movies about it," he concluded.

Earlier this week, Ben Affleck attempted to dismiss concern around Netflix's filmmaking process, in response to past comments from his long-term collaborator Matt Damon. At the same time, he also admitted Animals was riddled with AI elements , following his sale of an AI company to Netflix for around $600 million earlier this year.

articles.title: Kingdom Come: Deliverance Dev Hopes GTA 6 Will Encourage Studios to Charge More for Their Games
articles.summary: Warhorse co-founder Martin Klima wants GTA 6 to “blaze a trail” for higher game prices.
articles.body:
Warhorse co-founder Martin Klima wants GTA 6 to “blaze a trail” for higher game prices. Klima claimed triple-A games face an existential problem, with audience sizes plateauing, brick and mortar retail basically dead ("We destroyed retail, and we took all their money,” he said), and no new revenue streams to support the growing costs of making a big game.

Klima claimed that GTA 6 developer Rockstar and parent company Take-Two are in a unique position as the only companies "who can afford, or who can dare, to increase the price of games, which I think is long overdue and also necessary for this business to survive.

"The last thing you can do is to increase the unit price," Klima continued. "That would help a lot, but everybody's scared to death about it. Now, hopefully, GTA will blaze the trail, and it will allow us to increase the cost."

These comments come from an interview with PC Gamer , during which Klima admitted that GTA 6 “doesn't appeal to me at all” despite the series’ popularity. "I am not going to be playing GTA 6 unless I'm somehow forced to," he said. "And the reason why it is so popular — it beats me. It's something which I just fail to understand."

In the U.K., GTA 6 is priced £69.99 for the Standard Edition, which is pretty typical for a tentpole triple-A release. However, in the U.S. it’s $79.99 for the Standard Edition, 10 dollars higher than the usual price point of a new game. The Ultimate Edition, which includes in-game content most players will want, costs $99.99.

Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick previously commented on GTA 6’s price speculation, saying: “Consumers pay for the value that you bring to them, and our job is to charge way way way less of the value delivery. How you feel about something you buy is the intersection of the thing itself and what you pay for. Consumers need to feel like the thing itself is amazing and the price they were charged was fair for what they got.

“What we think about is making the most spectacular piece of entertainment on Earth, in history — and it’s a pretty daunting challenge. If we do that, and if we’re of service to our customers, then the upside will take care of itself.”

GTA 6 is widely speculated to be the most expensive game ever made, with Take-Two estimated to have spent between $1 billion to $2 billion developing and marketing the title. Yesterday, we wrote a story about a marketing stunt in Miami for GTA 6 that reportedly cost $1 million in itself.

The game is expected to be the most popular entertainment launch of all time, breaking records when it launches to the public this November. Analysts predict GTA 6 will generate $5.2 billion in sales by the end of launch week. GTA 6 releases for PS5 and Xbox Series consoles on November 19.
